title: Medieval and Early Modern Philosophy: Faith, Reason, and the Rise of Science

questions.question: Aquinas' five ways (quinque viae) argue by moving from:
options: Observed effects — motion, causes, contingency — to their first ground
questions.rationale: In the Summa Theologiae, each way starts from a feature of the world (motion, efficient causes, contingency, degrees of perfection, design) and traces it to a first source.

questions.question: 'What then is time? If no one asks me, I know; if I wish to explain it, I do not know.' This is:
questions.rationale: Augustine's meditation on time in the Confessions analyses it as a distension of the soul — past memory, present attention, future expectation.

questions.question: Ockham's razor states that:
options: Entities should not be multiplied beyond necessity
questions.rationale: The nominalist Ockham taught parsimony: prefer the explanation positing the fewest entities. He also held universals are mere names.

questions.question: Descartes' methodic doubt ends at the indubitable first certainty:
options: Cogito ergo sum — I think, therefore I am
questions.rationale: Doubting is thinking, and thinking requires a thinker — the cogito survives universal doubt, grounding the Meditations (1641) and his mind–body dualism.

questions.question: Spinoza's metaphysics holds that:
options: There are two substances, mind and body
There is one substance, called God or Nature (deus sive natura)
questions.rationale: Spinoza's substance monism: one infinite substance with infinitely many attributes, of which we know thought and extension; mind and body are two attributes of the same thing.

questions.question: Leibniz's monads are described as 'windowless' because:
options: They are too small to see
They do not causally interact; their harmony is pre-established by God
questions.rationale: Simple substances with no parts, monads unfold their states independently, coordinated by God's pre-established harmony in the best of all possible worlds.

questions.question: Locke's claim that the mind at birth is a tabula rasa means:
options: The mind contains innate mathematical truths
The mind is a blank slate written on by sensation and reflection
questions.rationale: In the Essay Concerning Human Understanding (1689), all ideas derive from experience — no innate ideas, against the rationalists.

questions.question: Berkeley's formula esse est percipi asserts that:
options: To be is to be perceived
questions.rationale: For Berkeley we perceive only ideas, never matter; things exist as perceived — ultimately sustained by God's perception.

questions.question: Hume's analysis of causation concludes that:
options: We observe only constant conjunction — B following A — and habit supplies the felt necessity
Causes are logical consequences of effects
questions.rationale: No observation reveals a necessary connection, only succession; the 'connection' is habit of mind. Hume likewise dissolved the self into a bundle of perceptions.

questions.question: Hobbes' Leviathan justifies absolute sovereignty because the state of nature is:
options: A golden age of natural harmony
A war of all against all, making life 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short'
questions.rationale: From fear, contractors surrender their power to an absolute sovereign; Locke's Two Treatises and Rousseau's Social Contract later moderate the idea.
